$comment: Where a catalogue variant could run on WaveSpeed instead of KIE.
Seed data for `pnpm providers:publish`, committed for the same reason
pricing.rows.json is: CI builds an empty database every run, so the rows
have to live in the repository.
EVERY ROUTE HERE IS SEEDED INACTIVE. None of these paths has been proved
by a call that returned 200 — there is no WAVESPEED_API_KEY in any
environment we control. `evidence` on each row says what is actually
known about it, and `scripts/spike-wavespeed.ts` is what turns that into
a fact. Activating a route before running the spike means finding out
The four are the ones the provider analysis found WaveSpeed actually wins
on, out of the seventeen models both can serve. Everything else stays on
KIE, including all of Veo — KIE bills it flat per generation while
WaveSpeed bills per second, so the cheap Veo tiers are 4-8x more

provider.name: WaveSpeed
$comment: creditUnitName is 'usd' because WaveSpeed prices in dollars rather than
in a credit of its own. That makes its provider_credit_rates row read
1.0 — one unit is one dollar — and a price row's providerUnits for a
WaveSpeed model is simply the USD price.

rates.note: One KIE credit. Verified twice against the live table: Veo 3 Fast 80cr = $0.40, Nano Banana Pro 24cr = $0.12.
WaveSpeed bills in USD, so its unit is a dollar.

routes.name: Qwen Image (WaveSpeed)
routes.evidence: path and every parameter read off wavespeed.ai/docs/docs-api/wavespeed-ai/qwen-image-text-to-image
routes.note: $0.02 on WaveSpeed against $0.02 of KIE credits; 4x cheaper and the coin price does not move, so the whole difference is margin.

paramOverrides.$comment: KIE takes aspect_ratio as a ratio string; WaveSpeed's qwen-image takes size as width*height. Renaming without translating would post '16:9' into a field that parses dimensions.

routes.name: Seedance 2.0 Fast (WaveSpeed)
